newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK TRADE WITH U.S. GOING DOWN, MINISTER SAYS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK TRADE WITH U.S. GOING DOWN, MINISTER SAYS.

text.p: Greek trade and business with the United States have taken a turn for the worse in the past three years and measures must be taken to reverse the trend, National Economy Undersecretary Alexandros Baltas said on Monday.
"The statistics for the past three years in our business and trade relations with the U.S. are not encouraging," he said.
He was addressing business leaders, officials and diplomats at a conference on the Greek economy organised by the American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce.

Greece's trade balance with the United States worsened in 1995 by 113.87 percent compared to 1994 and in 1996 the United States will be out of the top five export markets for Greece for the first time in decades, replaced by Bulgaria, he said.
"U.S. investments in Greece are also on the downside," he added. "These investments were extremely important in the first decades after 1953."
American investments in Greece total $1.25 billion. U.S. firms employ some 9,000 people in Greece, he said.
Baltas said lack of organisation in the public sector was the main factor discouraging foreign investors "but this problem can be resolved and will be resolved."

Baltas, responsible for Greece's foreign business relations, said the economy was in a recovery phase, with reduced inflation and interest rates, spending cuts in the public sector and a stable drachma.
"Exports and investments are the basic tools for Greece's development," he said. --Costas Paris, Intercontinental Newsroom, 30-1-9226961
